name.text: Calculating the Area of a Wheel Region

questiontext.text:
A wheel consists of a circular outer rim and a circular inner hub, both sharing the same centre \(O\), as shown below. The outer radius of the wheel is \({@R@}\,\text{cm}\), and the radius of the inner hub is \({@r@}\,\text{cm}\).

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-7, 7, 7, -7], axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); // Centre point, labeled so students see both radii originate here var O = board.create('point', [0, 0], { fixed: true, visible: true, name: 'O', size: 2, label: {offset: [-14, -12]} }); // Outer circle (rim) drawn first, fully shaded — represents the wheel material var outer = board.create('circle', [O, 5], { strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: 'black', fillColor: '#f5c518', fillOpacity: 1 }); // Inner circle (hub) drawn on top, filled white to "cut out" the centre // What remains shaded is the annular rim region only var inner = board.create('circle', [O, 3], { strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: 'black', fillColor: 'white', fillOpacity: 1 }); // Points marking the two radii var P_inner = board.create('point', [3, 0], {size: 2, fixed: true, visible: true, name: ''}); var P_outer = board.create('point', [-4, 3], {size: 2, fixed: true, visible: true, name: ''}); // Dashed radius segments, drawn last so they sit above the fills board.create('segment', [O, P_inner], {dash: 2, strokeColor: 'black', strokeWidth: 2}); board.create('segment', [O, P_outer], {dash: 2, strokeColor: 'black', strokeWidth: 2}); // Radius labels board.create('text', [1.2, -0.9, '{#r#} cm']); board.create('text', [-2.6, 0.9, '{#R#} cm']); [[/jsxgraph]]

Using \(\pi = 3.142\), determine the area of the wheel region (the shaded rim, excluding the hub). Give your answer correct to \(3\,\text{decimal places}\).

\(\text{Area of the wheel region}=\)[[input:ans1]]\(\,\text{cm}^2\)[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The outer radius (rim) is \(R={@R@}\,\text{cm}\).
The inner radius (hub) is \(r={@r@}\,\text{cm}\).

The area of the wheel region is the area of the outer circle minus the area of the inner circle:

\[ \begin{align} A &= \pi(R^2-r^2)\\ &=3.142\left({@R@}^2-{@r@}^2\right) \\ &=3.142\left({@R_sq@}-{@r_sq@}\right) \\ &=3.142 \times {@diff_sq@} \\ &={@A@}\,\text{cm}^2 \end{align} \]

Therefore, the area of the wheel region \(\approx {@significantfigures(A,3)@}\,\text{cm}^2\) (to 3 s.f.).

questionnote.text:
\(\text{The radius of the outer hub}={@R@}\,\text{cm}\)

\(\text{The radius of the inner hub}={@r@}\,\text{cm}\)

\(\text{The area of the wheel region}={@A@}\,\text{cm}^2\)

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.
